question: Does an authentic provider fence acknowledgement suffice to prove that a still-live old owner cannot cause a new effect after handover?
hypothesis: No. The observer must distinguish authentic issuer claims from atomic enforcement at the effect transaction.
fairness: Same copied R1 safety kernel, identities, grants, payloads, provider capabilities and causal schedules in both interfaces. This experiment isolates the provider boundary and does not supply the independent real-runtime integration requested elsewhere in R2.

provider_classes.atomic: Advertised and implemented atomic fence, valid-grant admission, idempotency and lookup in durable local SQLite.
provider_classes.opaque: Atomic fence and grant admission but no lookup and no idempotency; lost effect ACK remains UNKNOWN.
provider_classes.contract_violating_skip: Advertises same powers as atomic and signs real fence acknowledgement; intentionally omits current-fence check when executing.
provider_classes.contract_violating_split: Advertises same powers as atomic; validates old request, commits precheck, pauses, permits new fence, then executes without rechecking fence.

expected.atomic: stale request refused and no old effect
expected.opaque: stale request refused and no old effect
expected.contract_violating_skip: authentic fence accepted, then old effect observed; observer must report CONTRACT_VIOLATION

expected.atomic: real provider exit after COMMIT; new worker lookup recovers two obligations without duplicate
expected.opaque: one effect observed only by offline observer; runtime UNKNOWN, no blind retry

cases.name: expiry_while_old_worker_waits
cases.expected: real wall-clock expiry while separate old worker is alive; request refused at provider admission; no effect

cases.name: different_mission_id
cases.expected: request body mission_id differs from authentic grant; SCOPE_MISMATCH, no effect

expected.atomic: provider transaction blocks new fence until old effect commits; old effect precedes barrier, no violation
expected.contract_violating_split: new fence and active B established during pause; old effect follows barrier, observer detects violation

time: System wall clock; T03 grant TTL 2 seconds with receipt of readiness before expiration. No virtual clock and no independent host clocks.
processes: Provider RPC uses real Python subprocess and separate SQLite DB. Old-owner process remains alive on portable file gates. No network sockets, no SIGSTOP dependency, no claim Windows execution.
observer: Separate observe.py imports no copied runtime modules. Reads provider/coordinator SQLite read-only, independently checks HMAC fence receipt and its binding, compares causal event sequence and observed effect rows.
pass_criteria: All truthful-provider safety expectations and opaque UNKNOWN hold; both contract-violating providers produce causal counterexamples detected by the independent observer, in both interfaces. PASS on adverse cases means detection, never safe execution.
refutation: If signatures alone implied effect enforcement, no authentic-ack stale-effect counterexample could be observed. One valid counterexample refutes that inference; it does not refute cooperative-provider fencing.
scope_limits: same host and shared test key, not production identity or hostile-host isolation
local SQLite rows, not real business effects
deliberately faulted providers establish possibility, not prevalence
shared safety kernel makes equal outcomes expected, not a product comparison
bounded two-obligation fixture; no general memory migration or complete federation
allowed_actions: Local code, public-source-derived fixture and tests only; no contact, purchase, publication, new authority or modification of P06 R1.
